scope: Read-only investigation of the executed handoff failure. This JSON is the only new file written by this review; no jobs, signals, source, or prior evidence were changed.
prior_incorrect_assessment: scancel --signal=KILL --full 17777246 would deliver an uncatchable direct SIGKILL to the controller shell and Python, bypassing cancel_owned and leaving training allocations untouched.
correction: The job-level Slurm command cancelled the controller allocation through a termination path that delivered SIGTERM. The controller handled that signal and explicitly cancelled its separately allocated training jobs. My prior review confused scheduler cancellation semantics with a direct POSIX kill and gave an unsupported guarantee.

verified_local_evidence.finding: Records the exact --signal=KILL --full command, success return code, and immediate CANCELLED accounting state for job 17777246.
At 2026-10-09 12:52:50 Pacific, Slurm logs cancellation due to SIGNAL Terminated. Python then raises Campaign controller interrupted; no continuation authorized.
The old controller recorded cancel_owned targets 17777245, 17777247, 17777248, 17777249 and a successful scancel return.
R0_rerun_seed0 and NC1_seed1 terminated with Received SIGTERM after 138 saved rows, through iteration 137. Both retain all evaluations through 130, but lack training rows 138-139 and state_139.pt.

SIGTERM/SIGINT set interrupted; check_control raises; run except BaseException calls cancel_owned. The separately allocated training jobs were cancelled by this application cleanup, not by being children of the controller allocation.
Shell TERM/INT trap forwards TERM to the Python controller. The record does not distinguish direct Slurm delivery to Python from delivery via this shell trap; either reaches the same cleanup.

local_documentation.finding: --full includes batch script and its children. This recipient-scope statement alone does not prove that job-level KILL bypasses scheduler termination.

The notes distinguish the normal SIGCONT/SIGTERM/KillWait/SIGKILL cancellation sequence and special job-level KILL handling. I failed to establish the --full interaction before recommending the action.
KILL_STEPS_ONLY, KILL_JOB_BATCH, and KILL_FULL_JOB are separate flag bits; full does not imply either exception flag.

upstream_source_explanation.source_scope: Primary SchedMD upstream source for tag slurm-25-11-5-1, matching the installed reported version. Local slurmctld C implementation was unavailable; upstream sources were inspected through the web tool. No claim is made that local administrator patches were exhaustively ruled out.

sources.finding: For a running job, SIGKILL with neither KILL_STEPS_ONLY nor KILL_JOB_BATCH marks the job cancelled/completing and calls deallocate_nodes. KILL_FULL_JOB is not an exception. This explains why adding --full does not make this a direct uncatchable process kill.
The node termination handler resumes tasks with SIGCONT and normally sends SIGTERM to all active steps. This supports the controller log and explains how its cleanup handlers ran.

upstream_source_explanation.causal_conclusion: Observed TERM cleanup matches upstream scheduler cancellation semantics for SIGKILL plus KILL_FULL_JOB. It is not evidence that the operating system permits a Python handler to catch an actual delivered SIGKILL.

future_handoff_recommendation_not_execut.preferred: Implement an explicit cooperative controller handoff path that atomically stops new submissions, persists complete adoption state, releases its lock and exits without cancel_owned or finalization. Validate it with isolated fake scheduler tests and a disposable Slurm controller before relying on it for live runs.
future_handoff_recommendation_not_execut.direct_process_signal_alternative: A direct operating-system SIGKILL to independently verified controller process IDs on the controller node has different semantics from job-level scancel, but PID scope, shell trap behavior, race conditions and access must be verified first. No direct-kill command is validated or recommended for immediate execution by this review.
future_handoff_recommendation_not_execut.do_not_repeat: Do not use job-level scancel --signal=KILL --full as an assumed no-cleanup handoff mechanism.
